profiles.name: Jakhi McCray
profiles.description: Jakhi McCray (also recorded as Jakhi Lodgson-McCray), a young activist from Brooklyn, was charged in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of New York over a fire that destroyed ten New York City Police Department vehicles and a trailer in a secured lot in Bushwick, Brooklyn, in the early morning of June 12, 2025; the blaze caused an estimated 800,000 dollars in damage. He surrendered to authorities on July 21, 2025, was briefly detained, and was then placed on home detention in New Jersey. On April 8, 2026 he pleaded guilty to a federal arson charge, which carries a mandatory minimum of five years and a maximum of twenty years in prison. As of mid-2026 he remained free pending sentencing; his support committee reported that he spent about eight months on home detention before winning a modification to a curfew. His case is supported by Fire Ant Movement Defense.
profiles.finding: Reuters courtroom image and support committee social source found; NPPC article already has related image credit; source identity/crop pending.
profiles.rights: No image accepted; not assumed public domain

profiles.name: Lucas Griffith
profiles.description: Lucas Griffith, a student journalist interning for Cincinnati CityBeat, was arrested on July 17, 2025 while covering an anti-ICE march in Covington, Kentucky. He was held overnight and released the following day, July 18. Initially charged with felony rioting plus misdemeanors, he had the felony dropped and in October 2025 was convicted of one count of failure to disperse and acquitted of the others. He was fined fifty dollars plus court costs.
profiles.finding: CPJ article explicitly labels journalist image; original image download and credit verification lead.

profiles.name: Dario Sanchez
profiles.description: Dario Sanchez is one of the later-arrested defendants in the Prairieland prosecutions that grew out of the July 4, 2025 noise demonstration at the Prairieland ICE detention center in Alvarado, Texas. Not alleged to have been present that night, he is accused of evidence tampering for removing a person from Signal and Discord chats, and has been arrested three times in connection with the case. Across three separate detentions between July 15 and September 24, 2025 he spent roughly 43 days in custody before being released on bond; his case remains pending.
profiles.finding: KERA Sept25 case story and NewRepublic PDF portrait lead; Ecuador namesake excluded.

profiles.name: Lynette Sharp
profiles.description: Lynette Sharp is one of the defendants charged in connection with the July 4, 2025 demonstration at the Prairieland Detention Center, an ICE jail in Alvarado, Texas, which federal prosecutors charged as a "North Texas Antifa Cell" terrorism case. Pleaded guilty on November 19, 2025 to one count of providing material support to terrorists. Testified for the government as a cooperating co-defendant during the March 2026 trial. On July 1, 2026 they were sentenced to 110 months (9 years, 2 months) in federal prison.

profiles.name: Ginovanni Brumbelow
profiles.description: Ginovanni Joseph Brumbelow, 21, is an activist from Gresham, Oregon. On June 14, 2025 — No Kings Day, chosen to coincide with Donald Trump's birthday — he was arrested at a Portland protest against ICE immigration enforcement. He was charged with felony assault on a federal officer under 18 U.S.C. § 111(a)(1) and held approximately two days in federal custody before release pending trial. His case was among dozens arising from intensified federal prosecution of immigration-related demonstrators during the Trump administration's second term.
profiles.finding: Federal complaint includes case images; no clean independently identified portrait verified.

profiles.name: Morgan Lili Rykken
profiles.description: Morgan Lili Rykken was arrested during an anti-ICE protest in Portland, Oregon, on June 12, 2025. Portland police identified Rykken among ten people arrested that night and reported booking them into Multnomah County Detention Center. Rykken, a Gresham resident reported as 25, pleaded guilty to second-degree arson on December 3, 2025. The court imposed ten days in jail, five years of supervised probation, 200 hours of community service and $4,400 in restitution. Six additional charges were dismissed under the plea agreement. The prosecution concerned damage to surveillance equipment and a burning garbage container outside the ICE facility. The ten-day term is a sentence, not independently verified time served; the actual custody admission and release dates remain unresolved.
profiles.finding: Exact-name searches did not locate verified portrait in returned results; unresolved.

profiles.name: Christian Damian Cerna-Camacho
profiles.description:
Christian Damian Cerna-Camacho, a United States citizen from Boyle Heights in Los Angeles, was 28 when federal prosecutors accused him of punching a Customs and Border Protection officer during the June 7, 2025 protest against immigration raids in Paramount, California.

He was not arrested at the protest. Agents came for him four days later, on June 11, 2025, pinning his car between two unmarked vehicles on Whittier Boulevard in Boyle Heights with guns drawn and deploying a chemical device while his wife and their two young children were inside. The Department of Homeland Security then published its own high-resolution video of the operation on social media, calling him a “violent rioter” — footage which in fact showed him surrendering at once. Bail was refused at his first appearance, and he spent about a week in custody before being released to house arrest with GPS monitoring.

He pleaded guilty on December 16, 2025 to assault on a federal officer, a felony carrying up to eight years. At sentencing in 2026 the court rejected that framing. A federal judge described the department’s publicity campaign as a “vindictive effort” and “extrajudicial punishment”, the felony was reduced to a misdemeanor count of simple assault on a federal officer, and he received probation rather than prison.
profiles.finding: MyNewsLA case match uses stock house-arrest picture, not a subject portrait.

profiles.name: Mohammed Hoque
profiles.description:
Mohammed Hoque was a 20-year-old Bangladeshi international student at Minnesota State University, Mankato when he was first detained. In late March 2025, plainclothes ICE officers followed his car as he returned home from a coding class and surrounded him at his home, telling him his student visa had been revoked. He was held in ICE custody for over a month. He had no criminal record; the only basis the government cited was social-media activity, including Instagram posts about violence against Palestinians in Gaza and a #FreePalestine hashtag in his Instagram bio.

His attorneys filed a habeas petition arguing his detention was First Amendment retaliation for his support of Palestinian human rights. On May 7, 2025, U.S. District Judge Jerry Blackwell of the District of Minnesota ordered his immediate release, finding that Hoque's arrest aligned with the publicly stated executive policy of targeting social media users who express support for Palestinian human rights and criticise violence in Gaza. He was released on a 7,500-dollar bond.
profiles.finding: SahanJournal release report and FOX9 case coverage found; portrait verification pending.
